history.p: The song was written for the festivities in Rosenborg Garden on 30 August 1850 celebrating the return of the victorious Danish troops after the First War of Schleswig.

physDesc.physMedium: Eleven bars written on a piece of letter paper with three hand-ruled staves. Almost identical with the final version. For three voices. Above the third stave: "Mindet flyver som en Fugl hen til Slesvigs grønne". On the verso of the paper drafts for Hartmann's unfinished string quartet i G major. The paper is placed together with the autograph manuscript of this quartet.

physDesc.physMedium: Bound in brown cloth cover with black leather spine stamped with the monogram of King Frederik IX. In the middle of the cover, a black label with golden frame and golden letters inscribed: "J.P.E. HARTMANN / MINDESANG / OVER DE FALDNE". Written in brown ink. Paper: 20 staves. Above the music on p. 1: "Mindesang / over de Faldne" and the tempo marking: "Allegro moderato". Hartmann has only paginated the bifolios 1-4. Later paginated 1-14 in pencil at the bottom of the pages. With minor corrections in pencil and red ink. At the end of the music on. p. 14 Hartmann has written: "det med Blyant i 2den og 3die Vers antydede bruges naar Sangen udføres af Mandsstemmer alene."

Written in brown ink. Paper: 14 staves. Title above the music on p. 1: "Mindesang / over de Faldne" and tempo marking "Allegro moderato". The text of the first two stanzas is written beneath Tenori and Bassi, respectively. Pages 3-4 blank. Between stave 3 and 4 Hartmann has written "Messing" (Brass). Contrary to Hartmann's common practice, the text is written in Latin script.

annot.p: No. 1 in this collection. The original version had four stanzas. In this edition the third stanza, containing the line "Slesvigs Land er atter vundet" (The land of Schleswig has been regained), has been omitted, because it was published two years after Denmark having ceded Schleswig to Germany after the Second War of Schleswig. With the tempo marking Andantino.
